findings.title: Call to undefined zero-arg method breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the hierarchy is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) which requires one argument. There is no zero-arg overload, so the changed file does not compile. The intended call was likely isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()). Until fixed the module cannot build.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys disabled for anonymous first login
findings.body: New helper isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, and both authenticate and challenge(error,field) only call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when it returns true. Previously authenticate filled WebAuthn conditional-UI data when the user was not yet selected (anonymous first login) and challenge did the same when context.getUser()==null. After the change anonymous logins with user==null never set challenge, rpId, or ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, so the login page loses the webauthn form, username autocomplete, and discoverable passkey login. The correct condition for initializing conditional UI should not require a known user; it should be enabled for both first login and re-authentication.

findings.title: Only one of two display hooks disabled for conditional UI
findings.body: WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm uses shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to decide whether to populate ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS and separately uses shouldDisplayAuthenticators to set SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS. The subclass overrides only shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to return false, leaving shouldDisplayAuthenticators returning true whenever context.getUser()!=null. During re-authentication the form is therefore told to display authenticators while no authenticator list is provided, causing an empty/mismatched UI section instead of fully hiding it as the comment intends.
